text:
maya: heads-up: main is CI-red after I ran a poetry lock reorg to resolve a merge conflict. failing job: py3.9-integ. can someone quick-check? :grimacing:
build-bot: CI job failed: https://ci.internal.redwood/3490012345 py3.9-integ — pytest exit code 1
sam: thanks — pinging in case it's the usual transitive pin mess. any visible error in the logs?
maya: here's the failing trace (copied from the job):
```
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'Matcher' from 'rfc3986' (/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.12/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/rfc3986/__init__.py)

/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.12/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/httpx/_models.py:12
```
olga: hmm that smells like an rfc3986 API break. which packages pulled that in after the lock regen?
maya: lockfile diff shows these notable bumps: httpx 0.23.3 -> 0.24.0, rfc3986 1.5.0 -> 2.0.1, yarl unchanged.
liam: rfc3986 2.x bumped API surface — Matcher moved/renamed. probable transitive break in httpx or one of our vendored adapters.
nina: can we reproduce locally? maya, can you paste the exact venv steps you used in CI?
maya: same as CI: docker image python:3.9, pip install -U pip setuptools; pip install -r constraints.txt; run pytest -k integ -q
sam: quick triage plan: 1) try pip installing rfc3986==1.5.0 into a clean env with the current lock to confirm fix 2) run git bisect on the lockfile commit range 3) if confirmed, open a hotfix PR pinning rfc3986 or upgrade httpx to a compatible minor that expects rfc3986 2.x
olga: +1. also check whether any code imports Matcher directly — grep the repo for "from rfc3986 import Matcher"
liam: I can run the reproduce on my laptop in ~10m. if it fails locally we can quickly open a PR with a pin and run CI.
build-bot: triggered re-run: https://ci.internal.redwood/3490012345/2 (manual retry requested by sam)
maya: re-run came back same failure. looks deterministic.
nina: ok i'll grep and start a short bisect script suggestion:
```bash
# bisect candidate commits that changed poetry.lock
git checkout main
# list commits touching poetry.lock in last 5 merges
git log --pretty=format:%H -- poetry.lock | head -n 20 > /tmp/lock_commits.txt
# iterate and pip install the resulting constraints in a fresh venv (quick script)
```
sam: if someone can run `pip install rfc3986==1.5.0` into CI's test matrix and re-run, we can confirm it's the culprit before a PR. otherwise I'll try the bisect later tonight.
maya: here's a one-liner to test locally quickly:
```bash
python -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate && pip install -U pip && pip install httpx==0.24.0 rfc3986==1.5.0 && python -c "import httpx; print('ok')"
```
olga: if that prints ok then pining rfc3986 in constraints should be enough as short-term. long-term we should either upgrade httpx+deps or patch code to new rfc3986 API.
liam: ran the reproduce — import error replicates with rfc3986 2.0.1 + httpx 0.24.0. downgrading rfc3986 ->1.5.0 fixes it.
nina: opening quick PR that adds an explicit constraint `rfc3986==1.5.0` to constraints.txt and updates lockfile with that pin — will link in a sec.
build-bot: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/4582 (rfc3986 pin hotfix)
maya: great, thanks. @sam can you run full CI on that PR once green we can merge and cut a follow-up to plan for proper upgrade?
sam: yep i'll queue the full matrix. also logging a follow-up ticket to evaluate bumping httpx or adapting to rfc3986 2.x — assigning to eng-runtime.
olga: note for the follow-up: check any internal utility that may import Matcher directly; vendorized snippets might be hidden.
liam: thanks everyone. once PR passes i'll also scan other repos that depend on the shared constraints to avoid cascade surprises.
maya: short-term summary: cause = rfc3986 2.x API change introduced by lock regen; mitigation = pin to 1.5.0 in constraints + PR; long-term = upgrade httpx or migrate code to new API. :white_check_mark:
nina: PR CI is running now; will post results here.
build-bot: CI (PR 4582) status: running...
